name: @activepieces/piece-freshservice
description: IT service management software for ticketing, asset management, and IT operations.

auth.description:
To get your API key:
1. Log in to your **Freshservice** account as an agent.
2. Click your **profile picture** in the top-right corner.
3. Go to **Profile Settings**.
4. Your API key is displayed on the right side of the page.

For the domain, enter only the subdomain. For example, if your URL is **mycompany.freshservice.com**, enter **mycompany**.

api_key.description: Your Freshservice API key from Profile Settings.

create_ticket.name: create_ticket
create_ticket.description: Creates a new ticket in Freshservice.

description.description: HTML content of the ticket. You can use basic HTML tags for formatting.

type.description: The type of ticket (e.g., Incident, Service Request).

tags.description: Tags to add to the ticket.

custom_fields.description: A JSON object of custom field names and values.

aiMetadata.description: Opens a new IT service ticket in Freshservice on behalf of a requester. Use to log an incident or service request from an end user; requires a subject, an HTML description, and the requester (identified by id). Not idempotent — each call creates a separate ticket.

add_note_to_ticket.name: add_note_to_ticket
add_note_to_ticket.description: Adds a private or public note to an existing ticket.

body.description: The content of the note. HTML is supported.

private.description: If checked, the note is only visible to agents. If unchecked, the requester can also see it.

aiMetadata.description: Appends a note (conversation entry) to an existing Freshservice ticket identified by ticket id. The note can be private (agent-only, the default) or public (visible to the requester). Use to record an update or comment on a ticket. Not idempotent — each call appends another note.

create_requester.name: create_requester
create_requester.description: Creates a new requester (end user) in Freshservice.

first_name.description: The first name of the requester.

primary_email.description: The primary email address of the requester.

last_name.description: The last name of the requester.

job_title.description: The job title of the requester.

phone.description: The work phone number of the requester.

mobile_phone_number.description: The mobile phone number of the requester.

custom_fields.description: A JSON object of custom field names and values.

aiMetadata.description: Creates a new requester (end-user) record in Freshservice. Use to onboard a person who will submit tickets; requires a first name and primary email. Not idempotent — each call creates a new requester and will fail if the email already belongs to an existing requester.

request_ticket_approval.name: request_ticket_approval
request_ticket_approval.description: Requests approval for a ticket from a specified agent.

approval_type.description: How approval is determined when there are multiple approvers.

aiMetadata.description: Sends an approval request on a Freshservice ticket to a designated approver agent. Use when a ticket needs sign-off before proceeding; requires the ticket id and the approver agent id, and optionally sets whether all approvers or any one must approve. Not idempotent — each call raises a new approval request.

create_change.name: create_change
create_change.description: Creates a new change request in Freshservice.

planned_start_date.description: Planned start date and time (ISO 8601, e.g. 2025-01-15T09:00:00Z).

planned_end_date.description: Planned end date and time (ISO 8601, e.g. 2025-01-15T17:00:00Z).

custom_fields.description: A JSON object of custom field names and values.

aiMetadata.description: Opens a new change request (change management record) in Freshservice. Use to propose an IT change for planning, approval, and tracking; requires a subject and the requester id, with optional risk, impact, change type, status, and planned start/end dates. Not idempotent — each call creates a separate change.

update_change.name: update_change
update_change.description: Updates an existing change request in Freshservice.

planned_start_date.description: Planned start date and time (ISO 8601, e.g. 2025-01-15T09:00:00Z).

planned_end_date.description: Planned end date and time (ISO 8601, e.g. 2025-01-15T17:00:00Z).

custom_fields.description: A JSON object of custom field names and values.

aiMetadata.description: Modifies fields on an existing Freshservice change request identified by change id (e.g. subject, status, priority, risk, planned dates, assignment). Use to progress or revise a change; at least one field must be supplied or the call errors. Idempotent — re-sending the same field values leaves the change in the same state.

delete_change.name: delete_change
delete_change.description: Deletes a change request from Freshservice.

aiMetadata.description: Permanently deletes a change request from Freshservice, identified by change id. Use to remove a change that should no longer exist. Idempotent in effect — once deleted the change stays deleted, though repeat calls on an already-removed id may return a not-found error.

add_note_to_change.name: add_note_to_change
add_note_to_change.description: Adds a private or public note to an existing change request.

body.description: The content of the note. HTML is supported.

private.description: If checked, the note is only visible to agents. If unchecked, the requester can also see it.

aiMetadata.description: Appends a note to an existing Freshservice change request identified by change id. The note can be private (agent-only, the default) or public. Use to record commentary or an update on a change. Not idempotent — each call appends another note.

create_change_task.name: create_change_task
create_change_task.description: Creates a new task on a change request in Freshservice.

due_date.description: Task due date and time (ISO 8601, e.g. 2025-01-15T17:00:00Z).

notify_before.description: Time in seconds before the due date to send a reminder notification.

aiMetadata.description: Adds a task (sub-item of work) to an existing Freshservice change request identified by change id. Use to break a change into actionable steps; requires a title, with optional assignee, group, status, and due date. Not idempotent — each call creates a separate task.

update_change_task.name: update_change_task
update_change_task.description: Updates an existing task on a change request in Freshservice.

task_id.description: The ID of the task to update.

due_date.description: Task due date and time (ISO 8601, e.g. 2025-01-15T17:00:00Z).

notify_before.description: Time in seconds before the due date to send a reminder notification.

aiMetadata.description: Modifies fields on an existing task within a Freshservice change request, identified by change id and task id (e.g. title, status, assignee, due date). Use to progress or revise a change task; at least one field must be supplied or the call errors. Idempotent — re-sending the same field values leaves the task in the same state.

delete_change_task.name: delete_change_task
delete_change_task.description: Deletes a task from a change request in Freshservice.

task_id.description: The ID of the task to delete.

aiMetadata.description: Permanently deletes a task from a Freshservice change request, identified by change id and task id. Use to remove a task that should no longer exist. Idempotent in effect — once deleted the task stays deleted, though repeat calls on an already-removed id may return a not-found error.

custom_api_call.name: custom_api_call
custom_api_call.description: Make a custom API call to a specific endpoint

new_requester.name: new_requester
new_requester.description: Triggers when a new requester (user) is created in Freshservice.

aiMetadata.description: Fires when a new requester (end-user) record is created in Freshservice, representing a person newly onboarded into the help desk. Polls newest-first by creation time across all requesters in the account.

updated_requester.name: updated_requester
updated_requester.description: Triggers when an existing requester is updated in Freshservice.

aiMetadata.description: Fires when an existing requester (end-user) record is modified in Freshservice (e.g. profile, contact, or department change), representing the latest state of that requester. Polls newest-first by last-updated time across all requesters in the account.

new_change.name: new_change
new_change.description: Triggers when a new change request is created in Freshservice.

aiMetadata.description: Fires when a new change request is created in Freshservice, representing a freshly proposed IT change entering change management. Polls newest-first by creation time across all changes in the account.

updated_change.name: updated_change
updated_change.description: Triggers when an existing change request is updated in Freshservice. Note: newly created changes may also fire this trigger because their updated_at matches created_at.

aiMetadata.description: Fires when an existing change request is modified in Freshservice (e.g. status, risk, or schedule change), representing the latest state of that change. Polls newest-first by last-updated time across all changes; note that newly created changes can also fire this because their updated time initially equals their creation time.

new_change_task.name: new_change_task
new_change_task.description: Triggers when a new task is created on a specific change request.

aiMetadata.description: Fires when a new task is added to one specific change request in Freshservice, representing a newly created unit of work on that change. Scoped to a single change id chosen in setup; polls newest-first by creation time among that change's tasks.

sampleData.description: Assess the blast radius before proceeding.

updated_change_task.name: updated_change_task
updated_change_task.description: Triggers when a task on a specific change request is updated. Note: newly created tasks may also fire this trigger because their updated_at matches created_at.

aiMetadata.description: Fires when a task on one specific change request is modified in Freshservice (e.g. status, assignee, or due-date change), representing the latest state of that task. Scoped to a single change id chosen in setup; polls newest-first by last-updated time, and note that newly created tasks can also fire this because their updated time initially equals their creation time.
